parole.significato: An intoxicating beverage made by soaking the bark of the leguminous tree Lonchocarpus violaceus in honey and water and…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish balché, from Yucatec Maya balcheʼ.

parole.significato: A deep natural well or sinkhole, especially in Mexico and Central America, formed by the collapse of surface limestone…
parole.testo: From Spanish cenote, from Yucatec Maya tsʼonoʼot (“hole with water”).

parole.significato: A traditional Yucatec slow-roasted pork dish.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish cochinita pibil, a partial calque of Yucatec Maya píibil kʼéekʼen, from píib (“cooking pit”) + kʼéekʼen (“pig”).

parole.significato: A member or descendant of various peoples:
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish maya, from Yucatec Maya mayab (“flat”) or Yucatec Maya maaya, a self-designation of the northern Maya for themselves, in the form maya’ found in compounds and phrases e.g. maya’ wíinik (“Maya man”).
